title: WPSS/584/2016 of Rohit Kumar Shah Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
WPSS No.584 of 2016
U.C. Dhyani, J.
Mr. B.S. Negi, Advocate for the
petitioner.
Mr. Anil Dabral, Standing Counsel for
the State.
By means of present writ petition, the
petitioners seek following reliefs:-
(i) Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature
of certiorari quashing the order dated 20th
February 2016 passed by the respondent
no.2 insofar as it adversely affect the accrued
and vested rights of the petitioner for being
sent for training pursuant to his appointment
order dated 17th February 2014 and
subsequent selection/nomination order dated
2nd May, 2015 (communicated on 30th
December, 2015).
(ii) Issue a writ, order or direction declaring the
petitioner as eligible for Lekhpal Training
Course based on his appointment order dated
17th February 2014 and subsequent
selection/nomination order dated 2nd May
2015 (communicated on 30th December, 2015)
on the basis of prevailing Service Rules.
(iii) Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature
of mandamus commanding and directing the
respondents to forthwith send the petitioner
for Lekhpal Training Course based on his
nomination/selection vide communication
dated 2nd May 2015 (communicated on 30th
December 2015) and to grant all
consequential benefit including arrears of
salary.
(iv) Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature
of mandamus commanding and directing the
respondents to hold the Special Lekhpal
Training Course for the petitioner to ensure
that he is not denied his available rights due
to act of omission and commission by the
respondent State authorities and after
successful completion of Lekhpal Training the
petitioner shall be appointed as Lekhpal from
the date his junior is posted/appointed on the
said post with all consequential benefits.
It is the submission of learned counsel
for the petitioner that controversy in hand is
squarely covered by a decision rendered on
10.4.2017 passed by a coordinate Bench of
this Court in WPSS No.502/2016.
Learned State Counsel has fairly
conceded that present writ petition should be
decided in terms of decision rendered in
WPSS No.502/2016.

In view of the facts, narrated herein
above, the present petitioner should,
therefore, meet the same fate as was met by
WPSS No.502/2016.
 Accordingly, the present writ petition is
disposed of in terms of WPSS No.502/2016,
passed by a coordinate Bench of this Court
on 10.4.2017 to consider the petitioner for
sending to Lekhpal training at Almora within
four weeks.
[Pending application also stands
disposed of].
